novel_mechanics_found: Level 7 has four independently cycled sprite identities with period three: identical rendered color arrangements can hide different identity states, so frame deduplication alone is insufficient. Level 8 reveals three magenta movable pieces, three magenta-corner sockets, row switches that alter relative piece spacing, and a shared wrapping conveyor that can move a piece out of a socket rather than locking it.
narrative: The 52-click registry prefix reproduced level 5. A prior non-registry project provenance artifact supplied an L6 candidate tail; I replayed it live, observed level 6, then independently explored L7 from rendered frames. A directed ternary Gray-code sweep over the four identity controls found the L7 win, and the resulting 96-click full sequence passed reproduce() from a fresh reset with reached_level 7. I spent the remaining budget investigating L8, routed individual magenta pieces into sockets at several intermediate states, but did not find a simultaneous three-piece alignment before the 700-step session cap.
gotchas: The action that wins a level immediately renders the next level, so the solved board is not externally visible.
The left-edge vertical strip records clicks and changes the frame even when the puzzle arrangement cycles back; exclude it when comparing visible puzzle states.
On L7, two action histories can render identically while differing in sprite identity and win eligibility.
On L8, the shared conveyor wraps pieces out of completed sockets; sockets do not lock pieces in place.
